# LAW NO. 10/L-001 ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO FOR YEAR 2026

### LAW NO. 10/L-001 ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO FOR YEAR 2026

### LAW NO. 10/L-001

### ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO FOR

### YEAR 2026

Assembly of the Republic of Kosovo;

Based on Article 65, paragraphs (1) and (5) of the Constitution of the Republic of Kosovo, Adopts:

### LAW ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO

### FOR YEAR 2026

#### Article 1

Purpose The purpose of this Law shall be the definition of the budget appropriations of the Republic of Kosovo for year 2026.

#### Article 2

Scope The provisions of this Law shall be compulsory for all institutions and their respective units which fall within the scope of the Budget of the Republic of Kosovo for year 2026.

#### Article 3

Definitions

\1. Terms used in this Law shall have the following meaning:

Acronyms:

1.1. PAK - Privatization Agency of Kosovo;

1.2. KPCVA - Kosovo Property Comparison and Verification Agency;

1.3. GDP - Gross Domestic Product;

1.4. DTF - Development Trust Fund;

### LAW NO. 10/L-001 ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO FOR YEAR 2026

1.5. LMPFA - Law No. 03/L-048 on Public Financial Management and Accountability, amended and supplemented by Law No. 03/L-221, Law No. 04/L-116, Law No. 04/L194, Law No. 05/L-063, and Law No. 05/L-007;

1.6. POE - Publicly Owned Enterprises;

1.7. BO - Budget Organization(s);

1.8. PIP - Public Investment Program;

1.9. BDMS - Budget Development and Management System;

1.10. KFMIS - Kosovo Financial Management Information System;

Definitions:

1.11. Funds allocation - the maximum amount of commitments and expenditures which might be conducted in respect to specific budgetary allocations, as determined with envisaged procedures under Article 34 of LPFMA and registered at KFMIS;

1.12. Balance - amounts of unspent commitments, unallocated budget appropriations, uncommitted allocations and any revenues of a larger amount, larger than the expenditure and unspent commitments amount carried over from the previous fiscal year;

1.13. Total budgetary balance - defined as the calculation of the difference between the budgetary revenues and budgetary expenditures pursuant to Article 22.A of LPFMA

1.14. Source of funding - government grant (GG), own source revenues (OSR), and funding from borrowing within budgetary deficit (FB) and funding from borrowing over budgetary deficit or the Investment Clause (FBIC);

1.15. Budget of the Republic of Kosovo - the amount allowed by law which is in the disposal for expenditure from Kosovo Fund for a sub-program, specific purpose or, wherever a specific purpose is not identified, for an expenditure category of a budgetary organization, as provided by this law;

1.16. Liability - a legal agreement, such as the contract or „purchase order‟ in KFMIS, entered into by a Budgetary Organization, to make expenditures in the future;

1.17. Kosovo Fund - the Republic of Kosovo Fund established in accordance to the LMFPA in the accounts within the Central Bank of Kosovo and other commercial bank accounts which may be established by the Treasury and where all the public money, including collected interest, for the purpose of depositing or paying public money, provided

### LAW NO. 10/L-001 ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO FOR YEAR 2026

that this term shall not include any grant or donation from an international organization or foreign government, when the grant or donation is subject to the condition of not being included in the Consolidated Fund of the Republic of Kosovo;

1.18. Trust Fund - public money held by a budget organization within the Kosovo Fund, for the benefit of a person, body or enterprise that is not a budgetary organization;

1.19. Undistributed funds - the amount of money that has remained either unallocated and unspent in the Kosovo Fund till December 31st of the previous fiscal year;

1.20. Grants for budgetary support - revenues at Kosovo Fund from the transfer of funds from governments or other institutions for covering budgetary expenditures;

1.21. Investments according to the investment clause - means investments as determined under Article 22.A.7 of LPFMA, capital expenditures specified for the purposes of the investment clause;

1.22. Expenditure categories - categories “Wages and Allowances”, “Goods and Services”, “Utilities”, “Subsidies and Transfers”, “Capital Investments”;

1.23. Assembly - Assembly of the Republic of Kosovo;

1.24. Government – Government of the Republic of Kosovo;

1.25. Minister - Minister of Finance, Labour and Transfers;

1.26. Designated units - units included in the list A of LPFMA;

1.27. Budgetary Organizations - all ministries, municipalities, agencies and institutions, which receive budgetary allocations from Kosovo Fund pursuant to this Law;

1.28. Local Level Budgetary Organizations - implies the municipalities of the Republic of Kosovo;

1.29. Central Level Budgetary Organizations - all budgetary organizations excluding municipalities;

1.30. Employee position - a full-time position or the equivalent of a full-time position valid only for the education sector (teacher), where positions are considered based on the norm, converted into full-time employment, provided under table 2;

1.31. Budget receipts - all receipts in cash in Kosovo Fund;

### LAW NO. 10/L-001 ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO FOR YEAR 2026

1.32. Financial Regulations of MFLT - the Financial Management and Control Regulations, as defined in the LPFMA;

1.33. Reallocations - any changes that have occurred in tables 3.2., 3.2.B., 4.2. and

4.2.B., in the category of capital expenditures within a sub-program of a budget organization;

1.34. Kosovo Financial Management Information System (KFMIS) - the accounting record established within the Treasury of the Ministry of Finance, Labour and Transfer.

KFMIS, as used herein shall have the same meaning as the term “Treasury Accounting Record” which is defined in the LPFMA;

1.35. Budgetary expenditure - spending of cash from Kosovo Fund, excluding spending which increases financial assets, including the purchase of shares or financial rights, and excluding those spending that pays off financial obligations, including the recovery of debt principal;

1.36. Wage allowance– has the meaning as defined in Law No. 08/L-196 on Salaries in the Public Sector;

1.37. Budgetary spending - all spending in cash from Kosovo Fund;

1.38. Budgetary revenues - all receipts in cash which do not create financial obligations or not resulting from the decrease of financial assets of budgetary organizations;

1.39. Dedicated revenues - public money which is derived from a particular revenue source and is required by Law to be appropriated to an independent agency;

1.40. Non-tax revenues - all budgetary revenues excluding tax revenues or grants for budgetary support, which are collected for specific purposes pursuant to respective laws, including revenues from tariffs for permits and licenses, charges, penalties, dividends, interest, rents and concessions;

1.41. Tax revenues - all budgetary revenues which are collected in compliance with tax legislation in the Republic of Kosovo for funding of budgetary expenditures;

1.42. Own Source Revenues of Central Budgetary Organization - any form of public money, which is legally assessed based on cost recovery and collected as tariff and payment from central budgetary organizations, excluding revenues dedicated for independent agencies;

1.43. Municipal Own Source Revenues - any receipt of public money that has been assessed and collected by the municipalities from a source specified in Article 8 of the Law No. 03/L-049 on Local Government Finance;

### LAW NO. 10/L-001 ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO FOR YEAR 2026

1.44. Transfers - any change that has occurred within the approved appropriations presented in tables 3.1, 3.1.B, 3.2, 3.2.B, 4.1, 4.1.B, 4.2, and 4.2.B meaning the transfers which are:

1.44.1. the change of appropriated amounts between budgetary organizations;

1.44.2. the changes that occur between the sub-programs of the same budgetary organization; and

1.44.3 the changes that have occurred between each category of expenditures presented in Tables 3.1, 3.1.B, 3.2, 3.2.B, 4.1, 4.1.B, 4.2, and 4.2.B.

1.45. Fiscal year - period from the 1st January of a year to 31st December of the same year;

1.46. Commitments - projected expenditures, for which a Commitment Payment Order has been duly completed and submitted in accordance with the Treasury Financial Regulations and recorded in the KFMIS, whether or not they are subject to a legal obligation;

1.47. Loan for budgetary support - revenues at Kosovo Fund from the transfer of funds from the Government or by other international financial institutions for covering budgetary expenditures.

\2. Any terms used in this Law and not defined herein shall have the meaning assigned to them in the LPFMA.

#### Article 4

Approval of the Budget of the Republic of Kosovo for the Fiscal Year 2026

\1. Budget of the Republic of Kosovo for Fiscal Year 2026 shall be approved as determined in Table 2, and Tables 3.1, 3.1.B, 3.2, 3.2.B, 4.1, 4.1.B, 4.2, 4.2.B and 4.3, attached to this Law.

\2. Pursuant to Article 20 paragraph 8. of LPFMA, macro-fiscal projections for the Budget of the Republic of Kosovo for Fiscal Year 2026 shall be based on the updated macro-fiscal framework 2026-2028, and for informational purpose their description is attached to Annex 1 of this Law, along with performance indicators, that are attached to Annex 2.

\3. Medium-term fiscal projections, as well as allocations for the fiscal year 2026, with projections for two (2) following years, are summarized for information in Tables 1. and 1.1, attached to this Law.

### LAW NO. 10/L-001 ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO FOR YEAR 2026

#### Article 5

Budgetary appropriations of the Republic of Kosovo’s general budget

\1. The budget allocations from the Kosovo Fund for the Fiscal Year 2026, as presented in Tables

2., 3.1, 3.1.B, 3.2, 3.2.B, 4.1, 4.1.B, 4.2, 4.2.B and 4.3 attached to this law, shall be approved based on this law.

\2. The Ministry shall ensure maintenance of records of all approved budgetary appropriations, transfers and reallocations of budgetary appropriations and other approved adjustments to budget appropriations made during the fiscal year 2026 through the budget systems, KFMIS, and supplemented, if there are requirements, by other records in compliance with LPMFA. At least twice a year, during the review of the six (6) months report and final reporting on the closure of the fiscal year, the Minister assures that based on this register there is a report on budgetary amendments and adjustments that have occurred during the Fiscal Year 2026.

\3. Whenever it is requested by the Assembly, the Minister shall, on behalf of the Government, present to the Assembly a comprehensive report detailing and reconciling the approved budget appropriations for year 2026, and all subsequent transfers and other changes and the final budgetary appropriations for the Fiscal Year 2026.

#### Article 6

Municipal budget appropriations

\1. Notwithstanding Article 5 of this Law, budget appropriations in Table 4.1 that are based on the Municipal Own Source Revenues, shall be authorized for expenditure only after such revenues are deposited in the Kosovo Fund and duly recorded in the KFMIS.

\2. In cases when during the fiscal year, the amount of a municipality‟s own source revenue, which have been deposited into the Kosovo Fund and recorded in KFMIS, exceed the amounts of revenues appropriated in Table 4.1 of that municipality, Kosovo Treasury shall report such funds as available balances of the respective municipalities. These balances shall be available to fund activities and new or existing projects in current year, approved in accordance with procedures set out in the LPFMA.

\3. Municipal own source revenues from education shall be recorded separately and such revenues shall only be authorized and used by the municipality for education purposes only.

\4. Municipal own source revenues from primary health care co-payments shall be recorded separately and such revenues shall be authorized and used by the municipality for primary health care purposes only.

\5. Revenues that according to the legal authorization are collected by central-level budget organizations such as traffic fines, court fines, and similar, shall be allocated for expenditure in the respective municipalities every three (3) months.

### LAW NO. 10/L-001 ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO FOR YEAR 2026

\6. Part of this law includes the ceilings set for municipalities that have failed to approve the draft budget in time in their respective municipal assemblies due to local elections. If the municipal assembly approves and submits the proposed municipal budget for the fiscal year 2026 to the Minister after the legal deadline, and after the Assembly has approved the Law on Budget Appropriations for the Budget of the Republic of Kosovo for the fiscal year 2026, the Minister submits the proposed municipal budget to the Government for approval, provided that the budget is within the ceilings defined in the second circular and in this law.

#### Article 7

Own source revenues of central level budget organizations

\1. All own source revenues of central budgetary organizations shall be deposited by the central budgetary organizations into the Kosovo Fund and recorded in KFMIS in accordance with the Treasury Financial Regulations pursuant to the provisions in Article 5 of this law and the budget appropriations in Table 3.1 (a) for BO/s that have restrictions on the use of own source revenues respectively on the percentage of collected revenues which are allowed for spending, and (b)

central level own source revenues are authorized for spending without any restriction according to realization percentage, on a condition that such revenues are deposited in Kosovo Fund and are registered in KFMIS.

\2. In cases where during the fiscal year, the amount of own source revenues of an organization of central level, which have been deposited into the Kosovo Fund and recorded in the KFMIS, exceed the amounts of revenues allocated in Table 3.1, such revenues shall become general revenues in Kosovo Budget.

#### Article 8

Appropriation and re-appropriation of carried forward funds as well as the outstanding liabilities from previous year

\1. No later than thirty (30) days after entry into force of full budgetary appropriations for the Fiscal Year 2026, the Government shall submit a preliminary financial statement to the Assembly indicating the composition of fund balances for the Kosovo Fund from the fiscal year 2025, including:

1.1. unspent balances of the central budgetary organizations own source revenues;

1.2. unspent balances of municipalities‟ own source revenues;

1.3. unspent balances of the donor-designated grant;

1.4. balance of trust funds held by budget organizations;

1.5. funds that shall be kept as retained savings, and

### LAW NO. 10/L-001 ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO FOR YEAR 2026

1.6. unspent loans for designated entities.

\2. No later than thirty (30) days after entry into force of full budget appropriations for the Fiscal Year 2026, the Government shall submit to the Assembly for information a table showing the changes made in Tables 3.2, 3.2.B, and Table 4.2, requiring the budget organizations to fulfil the outstanding financial and contractual obligations from the previous year.

\3. The changes in Tables 3.2, 3.2.B, and Table 4.2 shall be limited as follows:

3.1. the total budget appropriation for capital projects, provided in Tables 3.1, and 4.1., for any budget organization, shall not increase as a result of these changes;

3.2. any other project added to Tables 3.2, 3.2.B and Table 4.2, must be a capital project that has been part of Table 3.2, 3.2.B and Table 4.2 of the Law on Budget Appropriations for year 2025.

\4. During budget allocation from the Treasury, priority shall be given to the allocation according to cash flow for the payment of liabilities reported as outstanding.

\5. Unspent balances of own source revenues of the central budgetary organization collected during the Fiscal Year 2025, deposited in the Kosovo Fund and recorded in KFMIS shall be appropriated for the fiscal year 2026, up to the level of their planning under Table 3.1 of the Fiscal Year 2025.

\6. Unspent balances of own source revenues of Municipalities from the fiscal year 2025 and previous years, deposited in the Kosovo Fund and recorded in KFMIS as the budgetary appropriation to a municipality, shall be appropriated for the fiscal year 2026 pursuant to LPMFA authorizations.

\7. Own revenues generated during the Year 2025 and registered in KFMIS that exceed the amounts of revenues allocated in Table 4.1 for Year 2025, shall be carried to Year 2026 in accordance with decision of the Municipal Assembly. Priority must be the allocation of funds for covering the existing contractual liabilities or liabilities deriving from final court decisions.

\8. Unspent balances from the Development Trust Fund from the fiscal year 2025 and previous years, deposited in the Kosovo Trust Fund and registered in KFMIS as budget appropriations for a municipality, at the request of the Mayor of the respective municipality, without changing the amounts and projects, shall be appropriated for the fiscal year 2026. These funds shall be recorded in KFMIS, as an unspent balance and municipalities shall be notified by the Minister.

\9. Unspent balances of designated donor grants, recorded in KFMIS, shall be appropriated for the fiscal year 2026 if there is a legally binding agreement in force.

### LAW NO. 10/L-001 ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO FOR YEAR 2026

#### Article 9

Appropriation of donor grants

\1. Pursuant to LPFMA, all donor grants shall be deposited into the Kosovo Fund and recorded in KFMIS unless otherwise required by the donor and if there is written consent by the Minister.

\2. After completion of the procedures according to Treasury Financial Rules, the donor grants shall be appropriated for the specified agreed purposes and may be allocated and spent for such purposes only.

\3. When a donor grant agreement expressly requires the donor to reimburse certain expenditures executed by a budget organization and by relevant budget appropriations, the full amount of the grant shall be appropriated after the execution of the grant agreement.

#### Article 10

Other budget appropriations

\1. All public money retained by the KPCVA in discharging its responsibility to design, implement and administer the rental scheme for the properties that the KPCVA has in its inventory and any respective payments from the KPCVA account shall be duly recorded in KFMIS and shall be considered as part of the Kosovo Fund in compliance with the legislative framework of KPCVA, LPFMA, this Law and the Treasury Financial Rules.

\2. All public money collected from goods imported from businesses registered in North Mitrovica, Zubin Potok, Leposaviq or Zveçan, which are intended for consumption in these municipalities, documented through relevant documents, at the moment of entry into Kosovo through customs points in Jarinje (point 1) or Brnjak (point 31) shall be sent to the Kosovo Fund by being identified and recorded in KFMIS, and allocated to the DTF created by the European Union Special Representative in Kosovo at the Commercial Bank which is licensed by the Central Bank of Kosovo.

\3. Unspent balance from previous years at DTF shall be appropriated for the fiscal year 2026 and transferred to beneficiary municipalities after approval of specific projects by the Management Board of this Fund. Regardless of defined provisions stipulated in Article 30 of LPFMA, the accumulated funds for the Development Trust Fund for year 2026 shall be transferred to beneficiary municipalities by the Minister, based on approval of specific projects by the Managing Board of this Fund, excluding expenditure category of “Wages and Allowances”, and changes are reflected in respective tables.

\4. The DTF amounts deposited in the Fund of the Republic of Kosovo and registered in KFMIS, category of capital investments, that are unspent, by decision of the Minister, such funds shall be registered as an available balance for DTF. The Minister shall, in an annual financial report, specifically report on appropriations and the way of using the funds for the Development Trust Fund.

### LAW NO. 10/L-001 ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO FOR YEAR 2026

\5. All trust funds shall be duly recorded in KFMIS and shall be considered as part of the Kosovo Fund in accordance with the LPFMA and the Treasury Financial Rules. Such Trust Funds shall be allocated for use on behalf of the designated beneficiaries.

\6. The amount of five million two hundred eighty-nine thousand seven hundred twenty euros (€5,289,720 €)) in the Ministry of Economy (ME) in the expenditure category of “Subsidies and Transfers” shall be dedicated to financing capital projects in publicly owned enterprises. Funds dedicated to finance capital projects shall be transferred to the publicly owned enterprises by the ME after the approval by the Inter-Ministerial Committee for publicly owned enterprises and the signing of the “Memorandum of Understanding” for this purpose between ME and beneficiary POE. This Memorandum of Understanding which is based on the decisions of the InterMinisterial Committee for publicly owned enterprises sets out the criteria for spending dedicated funds for capital projects, as well as the monetary rate appropriated for this purpose. These funds transferred for this purpose of spending shall not be used for operating expenses by publicly owned enterprises.

\7. Funds budgeted at the Office of the Prime Minister in the sub-program Support to Presheva Valley and Sanxhak shall be allocated by a decision of the Government with the purpose of supporting the Presheva Valley and Sanxhak.

\8. Funds budgeted at the Office of the Prime Minister in the sub-program Program for the Promotion of the Country are allocated by decision of the Government with the aim of organizing and supporting events or activities that contribute for the promotion of the country.

\9. Borrowing funds pursuant to the international financial agreement can be transferred or allowed for spending to the project implementer (publicly owned enterprise or public institution), through an understanding agreement between BO where the budget appropriation is, and the project implementer, after the approval by the Minister.

\10. The appropriated budget for the Office of Communities at the Office of the Prime Minister, expenditure category of subsidies and transfers, shall be used in compliance with the program for communities approved by the Government. The use of funds pursuant to this paragraph shall be done only after the approval of the program for communities by the Government.

\11. For the period January-December 2026, eight million nine hundred sixty thousand euro (8,960,000 €) shall be allocated to the Radio Television of Kosovo (hereinafter RTK), under the expenditure category of‟ “Subsidies and Transfers”. Before each six (6) months, RTK will submit the planned expenditure program to the respective Committee of the Assembly. At the end of each six (6) months, RTK shall submit to the Assembly a report on expenditures incurred. Funds under this paragraph shall be appropriated and transferred from the Treasury to the commercial bank account designated by RTK, according to the decision of the respective Committee on Budget. In the absence of a decision from the relevant Budget Commission, in order to ensure the continuity of the work of RTK (Radio Television of Kosovo), the Government may approve a temporary allocation, which must be adjusted and consolidated with the allocated limit according

### LAW NO. 10/L-001 ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO FOR YEAR 2026

to the decision of the relevant Budget Commission, whenever such a decision is made.

\12. Financial means allocated to the Ministry of Finance, Labour and Transfers in subprogram Agreements with bodies of the United Nations Organisation with code 34100 in category of expenditure Subsidies and Transfers with the Government decision can be transferred in BOs which through agreements with bodies of the United Nations Organisation aim implementation of projects and programs (commissions, funds and programs, specialised agencies and other entities) toward reaching of Sustainable Development Goals.

\13. Based on Law no. 08/L-305 on the Air Navigation Services Agency, all revenues collected by the Air Navigation Services Agency, recorded in KFMIS and unspent, are transferred to a commercial bank account designated by the Air Navigation Services Agency, except for amounts borrowed from the Kosovo Fund for the Air Navigation Services Agency in previous periods.

#### Article 11

Limits on commitments and expenditure

\1. No budget organization may exceed the total number of employees at the sub-program level, at any time during the Fiscal Year 2026 as specified in Tables 3.1, and 4.1 attached to this Law, except the women after childbirth and teachers with difficult health conditions in the pre-university education system. Any exceeding of the number of the allowed employees, except the women after childbirth and teachers with difficult health conditions in the pre-university education, and budget appropriations for each sub-program shall be considered a legal violation and legal measures shall be taken against the responsible persons according to the structure of the budget organization under the applicable legislation.

\2. In derogation from paragraph 1. of this Article, provided that the total number of the allowed employees and the relevant budget amount for the expenditure category "Salary and Wages"

within the budget organization do not change, the number of employees and the relevant budget amount for the expenditure category "Salary and Wages" under sub-programs in Tables 3.1, and

4.1, may be adjusted by Minister‟s approval with appropriate justification by BO, excluding the restrictions set forth in Article 14 of this Law. In regard to local-level BOs, a decision of the Municipal Assembly shall be required in advance. All approved changes in relation to the staff and the relevant budgetary amounts for the expenditure category "Wages and Allowances" shall be submitted to the Minister for updating Tables 3.1, and 4.1.

\3. In derogation from paragraph 1. of this Article in case of reorganization of BO as a result of new Government structure, the number of employees in BO in Table 3.1, may be adjusted by Minister‟s decision, after a justification provided by the responsible unit of human resources and approved by Chief Administrative Officer (CAO) of BO, under the condition that the total allowed number of employees in budget level should not be exceeded. All approved changes in relation to the staff shall be submitted to the Minister for updating Table 3.1.

### LAW NO. 10/L-001 ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO FOR YEAR 2026

\4. Notwithstanding paragraph 3. of this Article, in cases where the required number of employees for a budget organization is not sufficient within the total number permitted by this Law, the Government of the Republic of Kosovo is authorized, upon the proposal of the Minister, to decide on adjusting the permitted number of employees for budget organizations in accordance with the actual number of employees at the time of the adoption of this Law. This exception applies in situations involving changes to the structure of the Government.

\5. Following the approval of the new Regulation on the internal organization of the Government, by decision of the Government, the Minister is authorized to make the necessary adjustments to budget allocations and other relevant codes within the budgetary systems, including the transfer of expeditures to the new Ministries.

\6. Spending of public money from the expenditure category “Subsidies and Transfers” shall be limited to circumstances where there is a clear legal basis under this law, any other law, or any sub-legal act on such expenditures, and in no way paying allowances to regular employees under this category shall be permitted.

\7. Spending of public money from the expenditures category of “Goods and Services” shall not be permitted for payment of employees, either in the form of allowances or as contributions in goods, including meals or gifts, excluding reimbursement or allowed expenses for travels abroad, under the relevant legislation as well as excluding payment of university professors for provision of training services to teachers activity which is planned in the Ministry of Education, Science, Technology and Innovation (MESTI). This training is provided by respective university professors in accordance with memorandum of understanding between MESTI and the University of Prishtina (Faculty of Education) where this memorandum regulates procedures, deadlines, criteria, methods of payment and other needed details and is implemented in harmony with respective budget appropriations in MESTI.

\8. BO shall not announce a tender for a capital project approved in Tables 3.2, 3.2.B, 4.2 and

4.2.B, after 31 October 2026 for potential expenditure in the fiscal year 2026, unless those expenditures are planned for that capital project and subsequent years specified in Tables 3.2,

3.2.B, 4.2 and 4.2.B.

\9. Signing contracts for multi-year capital projects shall be signed by BO only if such expenditures for the total cost of the project are provided for in the law on budget appropriations for the fiscal year 2026 and the two (2) following years. If a capital project is planned to be implemented beyond three (3) years covered by this law, then such approval shall be granted by the Government.

\10. Each BO must register in PIP and KFMIS its multi-year contractual obligations for capital projects, as well as upload in PIP and KFMIS contracts for capital projects that are part of budget tables of this law.

\11. If an individual, official, person or entity receives any payment from the Kosovo Fund as a

### LAW NO. 10/L-001 ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO FOR YEAR 2026

result of a mistake, error or omission, those funds shall be returned to the Kosovo Fund within five (5) days of receipt of the written notice from the Director General of the Treasury notifying the receiving party that the payment had been made in error:

11.1. in cases where a budgetary organization notices that a payment has been made incorrectly, it shall immediately inform the Director General of the Treasury and a return order shall be issued immediately;

11.2. in cases where a payment has been made incorrectly and no return has been made, the Director General of the Treasury has full authority to use the necessary legal remedies for the return of wrongly paid funds, including freezing of bank accounts in which wrongly paid funds are transferred, until court decision.

#### Article 12

Advance payments

\1. BOs may make advance payments to contractors for capital projects and goods and services up to fifteen percent (15%) of the contract value. Such advance payment may be made only on the basis of a legally concluded contract, with a value of more than ten thousand euro (10.000 €), which has been achieved in accordance with the Law on Public Procurement. For the advance payment for capital projects, the contract must contain the performance guarantee and a clearly defined payment schedule, which at the same time foresees the work to be performed before making each payment.

\2. The Government may approve the advance payment in the amount of up to thirty percent (30%) of the contract value for capital projects.

\3. The Government may approve the advance payment of more than thirty percent (30%) and up to one hundred percent (100%) of the contract value for goods and services.

\4. In derogation from paragraphs 1., 2. and 3. of this Article, in November 2026 the advance payment shall be limited to ten percent (10%) and in December 2026 up to five percent (5%) of the contract value.

\5. Advances of up to one hundred percent (100%) from the budget appropriation of the current year shall be allowed for projects and activities related to the defence and security of the Republic of Kosovo. Advances related to projects and activities on defence and security of the Republic of Kosovo shall be allowed to remain open for subsequent years for those projects for which the delivery of equipment cannot be done within a regular fiscal year.

\6. In cases of the provision of grant schemes/subsidies for natural and non-public legal persons, in accordance with paragraph 5. of this Article, the budgetary organisation can issue sublegal act where transfer as a pre-payment to contractors-beneficiaries of up to fifty per cent (50%) of the means from the value of the grant contract is regulated. Such advance payment, if applicable,

### LAW NO. 10/L-001 ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO FOR YEAR 2026

can only be made based on a legally concluded contract in accordance with sectoral legislation as well as that of public finance, provided that before the advance payment of the grant, a bank advance guarantee is accepted (at inspection - unconditional) at one hundred percent (100%) of the value to be transferred and for the full term of the contract. BO shall be an unconditional beneficiary of the bank guarantee.

\7. In derogation from paragraph 6. of this Article, the Government may approve a sub-legal act which regulates the advance payment up to one hundred percent (100%) of the value of the grant scheme according to the relevant sectoral legislation. In this case, the bank advance guarantee shall apply appropriately (one hundred percent (100%) of allowed advance).

\8. BOs may make advance payments to employees travelling outside the Republic of Kosovo in accordance with applicable legislation on travelling abroad and in accordance with Treasury Financial Regulations. For travelling abroad, advances shall be transferred to the public official's account through the banking system. Such advances shall be closed and the unspent amounts shall be returned to the Kosovo Fund, in accordance with the Treasury Financial Regulations.

The quota for small expenses (pocket money) is a component of the official travel advance payment and are not considered as a taxable income.

\9. If advances for petty cash or travels made during 2025 are not closed before 15 January 2026 in accordance with Treasury Financial Rules, expenditures related to these advances shall be recorded in the budget appropriations for year 2026. If the advances for Diplomatic and Consular Missions incurred during the year 2025 are not closed before 27 January 2026 in accordance with the Treasury Financial Rules, the expenses related to these advances shall be recorded against the budget appropriations for the year 2026.

#### Article 13

Unforeseen expenditures and reserves

\1. The unforeseen expenditures shall be appropriated under the subprogram: “Unforeseen Expenditures” in Table 3.1 and these funds shall be allocated in accordance with Article 29 of the

### LPFMA.

\2. The Minister shall be authorized to approve transfers from the sub-program “Unforeseen Expenditures” to any other sub-program in Table 3.1 and Table 4.1, for individual amounts requested up to the value of forty thousand euro (40,000 €). The cumulative amount of allocated funds of this authorization may not exceed twenty percent (20%) of the allocated annual amount of the sub-program “Unforeseen Expenditures”.

\3. Funds allocated to the Ministry of Local Government Administration, under the code 212, in the capital project “Municipal program for the development of socio-economic infrastructure and inter-municipal cooperation” under code 15633 and the capital project “Program for municipal performance-based grants” with code 20659, can be reallocated to new capital projects after approval by the Government in accordance with the memorandum of understanding signed

### LAW NO. 10/L-001 ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO FOR YEAR 2026

between the Minister of the relevant Ministry and the Mayor of the respective municipality.

\4. Funds allocated to the Ministry of Regional Development, under code 221, in the capital project “Regional Development Program” under code 18782, can be reallocated to new and existing capital projects after approval by the Government in accordance with the memorandum of understanding signed between the Minister of the relevant Ministry and the Mayor of the respective municipality, and by the donor as appropriate.

\5. Funds allocated in the Ministry of Environment, Spatial Planning and Infrastructure under code 205, in the capital project “Co-funding program with the municipal assembly” under the code 10041 can be reallocated to new capital projects after approval by the Government in accordance with the memorandum of understanding signed between the Minister of the relevant Ministry and the Mayor of the respective municipality, and by the donor as appropriate.

\6. Funds allocated to the Ministry of Culture, Youth and Sports (MCYS) under code 207, in the capital project “Preventive measures, emergency interventions” under code 12688 can be reallocated to new projects after approval by the Government, as MCYS specifies the location for intervention in the area of cultural heritage. New capital projects created under this paragraph must receive the relevant budget codes. The limitations provided for in Article 15 of this Law shall not apply to this paragraph.

\7. The Minister responsible for Agriculture, Forestry and Rural Development shall be authorized, through a sub-legal act, to implement the subsidy and grant schemes for (i) the Rural Development Program for year 2026 and (ii) the Program for Direct Payments for year 2026, according to the budgetary allocations in Table 3.1. attached to this Law and the restrictions in Article 12 of this Law.

\8. The Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Rural Development (MAFRD), under code 203, after the natural damages created in agriculture, shall allocate the funds directly to the farmers affected by the sub-program “Natural damages in agriculture” under the code 47600, category of expenditures “Subsidies and Transfers”, after the approval by the Government of the report regarding the damages incurred.

#### Article 14

Transfer of allocated budgetary amounts

\1. The transfer of allocated budgetary amounts shall be done in accordance with Article 30 of the LPFMA, at the level of the budget sub-program and the category of expenditures, according to the criteria and procedures provided by sub-legal acts in force. The percentage of the calculation of the negatively affected budget allocation shall include all sources of funding. Transfers up to five percent (5%) of a budget appropriation to other appropriation of the same budget organisation during the whole fiscal year is allowed without obtaining permission from Minister in cases where justification of transfer is provided by Chief Administrative Officer.

### LAW NO. 10/L-001 ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO FOR YEAR 2026

\2. The Minister may allocate funds provided by the Ministry of Finance, Labour and Transfers, under the program “Contingencies in the Ministry of Finance, Labour and Transfers”, in all categories of budget expenditures, after approval by the Government. Funds from “Contingencies in the Ministry of Finance, Labour and Transfers” can be allocated also for payment of funds declared as donations to international financial organizations, covering payment guarantees for renewable energy projects by KOSTT, as well as for covering financial impact of the new laws that enter into force during 2026, including formation of programs and subprograms that are foreseen by the new law entered into force.

\3. Three million euros (3,000,000 €) have been budgeted in the Ministry of Finance, Labour and Transfers under the sub-program of the Central Administration with code 11301, which will be used for the reimbursement of funds withdrawn from the Kosovo Pension Trust by the citizens of Kosovo based on Article 5 of the Law No. 07/L-016 on Economic Recovery-COVID 19.

\4. When the budget organization has under-expenditure compared to the cash flow plan submitted to the Treasury, the Minister may, during the last three (3) months of the fiscal year with the prior approval of the Government, after receiving a valid justification from requesting BO, authorize the reduction of the budget allocation for all categories of expenditures of that BO, excluding own source revenues, dedicated revenues and borrowings, transfer it within the same budget organization or transfer that allocation to other BO, by excluding all paragraphs and Articles which restrict budget transfers. These funds shall not be transferred for new capital projects. The cumulative value of all these transfers according to this paragraph shall not exceed five percent (5%) of the total value of all budget appropriations where in this percentage are not calculated changes in budget appropriations incurred by September 30 of the fiscal year.

\5. The calculated percentage of budget appropriations negatively affected according to paragraph 2. of this Article shall be excluded from the percentage of transfers which are regulated under Article 30 of the LPFMA and this article.

\6. In derogation from paragraphs 2. and 4. of this Article, no transfer of budget appropriations may be made in the category of “Wages and Allowances” from any other category of expenditures without prior approval of the Assembly. Exceptionally, in the last three (3) months, the transfer is allowed in accordance with Article 30 of the LPFMA from the other categories in category of “Wages and Allowances” only in cases where such shortage in category of “Wages and Allowances” comes as a result of execution of court orders or final enforcement decision.

\7. The transfer of budgetary allocations within the category of “Wages and Allowances” can be done between sub-programs of the same BO with the approval of the Minister. Such transfers of municipalities shall require prior approval from the Municipal Assembly. Such transfers shall not be subject to the limitations of budgetary transfers of any paragraph or sub-paragraph restricting such transfers.

\8. Prior approval by the Assembly is required for any transfer between BOs except for paragraphs 2. and 4. of this Article.

### LAW NO. 10/L-001 ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO FOR YEAR 2026

\9. After the approval of each transfer, the adjustment of the allocated amounts shall be done in Table 3.1. and Table 4.1. and shall be recorded in KFMIS.

\10. The budget allocations from the "Reserve" shall be appropriated into the category of capital investments, after the BO gives a rationale for the capital project proposal according to the sublegal acts in force. The transfer of funds from the “Reserve” according to the rules of this paragraph can be done after the approval of the Chief Administrative Officer and the Chief Financial Officer and in the case of the municipality after the approval by the Municipal Assembly.

These budget moves shall not be subject to the transfer restrictions contained in Article 30 of the LPFMA and Articles 14 and 15 of this Law.

\11. Notwithstanding paragraph 10. of this Article, in case of municipality, budget appropriations from “Reserve” with priority are allocated to respective category of expenditures for meeting court and enforcement decisions by the decision of chief administrative officer.

\12. Transfers and reallocations according to Article 30 of LPFMA and Articles 14 and 15 of this law are allowed even in cases where before the initiation of procurement procedure the budget organisation in order to provide the statement of availability of funds conducts a professional and competent estimation of realistic potential costs regarding the implementation of certain project or activity.

\13. The Minister is authorized, upon receipt of funds from the loan under the Growth Plan in the Treasury account, to transfer them to the Common Fund of the Western Balkans European Union (EWBJF), established within the framework of the Western Balkans Investment Framework (WBIF), in accordance with the contribution agreements between the Republic of Kosovo and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, as well as the European Investment Bank, in line with the general rules and conditions applicable to the fund. The authorization takes effect after the ratification of the Loan Agreement between the Republic of Kosovo and the European Union for the "Mechanism for Reform and Growth for the Western Balkans."

#### Article 15

Changes in amounts allocated to capital projects under subprograms

\1. Funds can only be allocated to the capital projects listed in Table 3.2. For capital projects presented in Table 3.2, the Minister may, if provided with valid justifications by the head of BO, authorize the movement of funds allocated from one capital project to another within the same sub-program of such BO, provided that the amount carried forward is less than or equal to fifteen percent (15%) of the total value of the approved “Capital Investment” category for that subprogram. Reallocations must be carried out in accordance with the procedures and criteria provided by the sub-legal acts in force.

\2. For each capital project presented in Table 3.2, the Minister may, if valid justifications are provided by the head of BO, submit a request for approval to the Government for the transfer of

### LAW NO. 10/L-001 ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO FOR YEAR 2026

funds allocated from one capital project to another within the same sub-program of such BO in the amount higher than fifteen percent (15%), but less than twenty-five percent (25%) of the total value of the “Capital Investment” category approved for that sub-program.

\3. For each capital project presented in Table 3.2., after approval by the Government, the Minister shall submit a request for approval to the Assembly, for the movement of funds allocated from one capital project to another within the same sub-program of such BO in the amount equal to or higher than twenty-five percent (25%) of the total value of the “Capital Investment” category approved for that sub-program.

\4. The percentage of the calculation of the negatively affected budgetary allocation of paragraphs

1., 2. and 3. of this Article shall include all sources of funding.

\5. New capital projects at the local level may be added, provided that such capital project is fully financed from the undistributed balances of carried forward revenues and allocated for the fiscal year 2026.

\6. New capital projects can be added to Table 3.2 and Table 4.2, provided that they are financed according to the procedures authorized in paragraph 2. of Article 6, paragraph 5. and paragraph

\8. of this Article if they become part of the PIP in accordance with the sub-legal acts in force.

\7. For the purposes of paragraphs 1., 2. and 3. of this Article, the head of BO shall prepare a valid justification, which shall contain a rationale that the estimated cost of the capital project is higher than the available funds which are determined in accordance with the Law on Public Procurement, or that a capital project needs fewer funds than the amount specified in the budget appropriations.

\8. New capital projects can be added to Table 3.2 and Table 4.2 in the following cases:

8.1. when existing projects are fully or partially funded by donors, insofar as funding for new projects does not exceed the amount of donor funding for the existing project;

8.2. in case of participation of the community and/or other donors in the co-funding of a project at the local level in which case a new project code is created after approval by the Municipal Assembly, in this case, the new project can be created with funds from the cofunding project code based on the memorandum of understanding between the municipality and the community/donors;

8.3. when there are funds left over from existing projects that are physically and financially completed, new capital projects can only be added as long as there is a surplus of left over funds;

8.4. when the existing project fails to be implemented due to property and legal problems;

### LAW NO. 10/L-001 ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO FOR YEAR 2026

8.5 when the projects are financed by the DTF; and

8.6. when the Government decides according to Article 29 of the LPFMA.

\9. For every new capital project that is added to Table 4.2, prior approval from the Municipal Assembly shall be required.

\10. Each BO when proposing new capital projects for inclusion in the annual budget appropriations, must complete all the data required in the PIP and in sub-legal acts in force.

\11. Changes in allocated budget amounts for existing projects as a result of transfers and/or reallocations, presented in Table 4.2, including the carried forward own source revenues and projects registered in KFMIS, must be approved in advance by the Municipal Assembly, whereas in the case of TDF the changes in the allocated budget amounts must be approved by the TDF Board. All these changes shall be approved by the Minister.

\12. The Minister shall be authorized to adjust the allocated budget amounts for capital projects with a source of funding from the „Investment Clause‟ depending on the progress and dynamics of work, limited only to (i) projects that are part of the list under this Law or become a part thereof under Article 23 of this Law and (ii) up to the loan amount according to the agreement ratified by the Assembly for the project in question, upon recommendation by the Minister of the Ministry or the mayor of the implementing municipality of the project and approval by the Minister. Such a change shall not affect the deficit limit according to the fiscal rule and is not subject to the transfer restrictions contained in Article 30 of the LPFMA and Articles 14 and 15 of this Law.

#### Article 16

Budget execution

\1. The Chief Administrative Officer of BO shall be the main legal responsible person for budget execution, in accordance with Article 10 of the LPFMA as well as sub-legal acts approved by the Minister, including the delegation of expenditures to BO. In the case of technical errors made by the BO during the preparation of the budget, which are not of a material nature and have become part of the budget tables of this law, the Chief Administrative Officer of the BO may request their correction from the Minister after providing justification. In the case of the local level, prior approval from the municipal assembly is also required.

\2. All Chief Financial Officers shall (i) ensure the drafting of the budget proposal and request for budget appropriation of the relevant budget organization or autonomous executive agency; (ii)

ensure that all transactions are recorded in the Treasury Accounting Register; (iii) ensure that all regular invoices received by the budget organization are immediately submitted for payment through the Treasury system; (iv) ensure the supervision of all aspects of budget reporting by the budget organization; and (v) ensure the exercise of all the functions given to the CFO according to the sub-legal acts.

### LAW NO. 10/L-001 ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO FOR YEAR 2026

\3. The Treasury of Kosovo, through KFMIS, shall report on a quarterly basis for budget execution, which includes the execution of capital projects approved by this law, in accordance with Article 45 of the LPFMA.

\4. All BO shall, through PIP system, report to the Ministry of Finance, Labour and TransfersBudget Department, within three (3) weeks from the end of each quarter for the physical and financial progress of capital projects, with total value (for all years) over one million euro (1,000,000 €).

\5. The Chief Financial Officer of each municipality shall submit to the Mayor within three (3)

weeks from the closure of each three (3) months a detailed report on the progress achieved in the implementation of all capital projects worth more than ten thousand euro (10,000 €). A copy of such report must also be submitted to the Minister.

\6. Every central-level BO that funds or co-funds local-level projects on regular municipal funding must implement clear, fair and transparent criteria. The central Budgetary Organization and the beneficiary municipality shall sign an agreement which regulates the obligations of both parties regarding the procurement process, implementation and supervision of the project, settlement of obligations, completion and technical acceptance of the project, as well as asset registration.

Agreements under this Article must be in line with the budget possibilities of budget financing or co-financing organizations and shall be authorized in advance by the Minister.

\7. Appropriations of funds shall be allowed on a quarterly basis, for the entire fiscal year at once for the purpose of committing funds, as long as funds are spent on a monthly basis based on the cash inflow planned in the relevant module in KFMIS, in accordance with sub-legal acts. The unspent balances from the monthly sub-allocation of the planned cash flow in the relevant module in KFMIS are carried over from month to month within a quarter if the monthly bank balance and cash flow allows the Treasury to act as such.

\8. The Ministry of Finance, Labor, and Transfers (MFPT) creates the new capital project code and the appropriate sub code according to the chart of accounts for the execution of court as well as enforcement decisions. The necessary budgetary funds for the creation of the new project are secured from another capital code of the budget organisation, whereby the negatively affected amount is reflected.

#### Article 17

Budgetary Impact Assessments for new initiatives

\1. Whenever a new initiative is proposed, including new legislation, a strategy or any other similar act, the proposing body shall submit it in advance to the Ministry of Finance, Labour and Transfers along with the Budget Impact Assessment Form. The Ministry of Finance, Labour and Transfers shall make a detailed assessment of the impact it may have on the Kosovo Budget for at least the next three (3) fiscal years.

### LAW NO. 10/L-001 ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO FOR YEAR 2026

\2. The proposing body according to paragraph 1. of this Article must obtain an opinion on the budget impact assessment from the Ministry of Finance, Labour and Transfers regarding the budgetary impacts of the proposed legislation before submission to the Government and the Assembly for review and approval.

\3. The Budget Department, if necessary, in cooperation with the Department on Economic Policy, shall review the Budgetary Impact Form according to paragraph 1. of this Article, and present their independent opinion regarding the validity of the budgetary impact calculation, the availability of funding sources in accordance with this Law, before the Government or the Assembly when the proposer is the Assembly.

\4. Any new initiative for expenditure, including the proposed new legislation, that does not have a budget allocation included in the attached tables, shall not receive a budget allocation unless appropriate cuts are made to other budget allocations of the same value.

\5. No draft law may be submitted to the Government or the Assembly for approval if it has not identified the source of funding for Fiscal Year 2026 and subsequent years provided in the Medium-Term Budget Expenditure Framework 2027-2028 foreseen in Article 5, paragraph 1., and tables within this Law.

\6. No decision of the Government on new initiatives that may produce a financial liability for the fiscal year 2026 can be legally binding if the same does not identify the source of funding provided by the allocations under Article 5, paragraph 1. of this Law, or if it does not identify the necessary savings and cuts in existing allocations in accordance with the LPFMA and paragraph 4. of this Article.

\7. If the Government approves a new initiative that produces budget obligations for one or more budget organizations after the fiscal year 2026, then this budget obligation shall be automatically addressed in determining the allocations for these BO during the preparation process of the budget for the following year.

#### Article 18

Supervising the implementation of projects

\1. In order to implement and supervise projects financed by borrowing and other projects of interest to the Republic of Kosovo, at the proposal of the Minister of the relevant Ministry, the Minister may decide to allow compensation of relevant experts that are not part of the list of employees of any BO that receive salaries from Kosovo Budget, to supervise the implementation of such projects in accordance with the applicable legislation on state debt. In this case, the source of their funding is provided.

\2. Supervision of the implementation of the financed projects according to paragraph 1. of this Article, can be done only if it is not foreseen otherwise with the loan agreement.

### LAW NO. 10/L-001 ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO FOR YEAR 2026

\3. BO implementing one or more projects financed under paragraph 1. of this Article, may establish one unit that is engaged with implementation of one or more projects at the same time.

#### Article 19

Funds for the maintenance of emergency liquidity assistance In accordance with the provisions specified in Table 1., based on the Memorandum of Understanding for Emergency Assistance, signed between the Governor of the Central Bank, the Minister and the Chairman of the Committee on Budget, Labour and Transfers of the Assembly, forty-six million euro (46,000,000 €) shall be retained from the Government balance sheet as a reserve in case of emergency to maintain the liquidity of the financial system.

#### Article 20

State Debt Service

\1. The Kosovo Treasury shall be authorized to execute transfers on behalf of the state debt service from the Kosovo Fund, in accordance with the legislation on state debt.

\2. The value of transfers for state debt service shall be calculated by the Ministry based on agreements in force and in accordance with the relevant law on state debt.

\3. The indicative forecast of the value of transfers for interest expenses shall be presented in Table 1 and Table 2 attached to this Law and shall be treated as part of the general budget expenditures.

\4. The indicative forecast for outflows on behalf of the return of principal shall be presented in Table 1. attached to this Law as part of the receipts and outflows provided for financing the budget deficit.

\5. In derogation from paragraphs 3. and 4. of this Article, in the event of changes in market conditions or exchange rates, the Ministry shall transfer the necessary funds for the state debt service pursuant to paragraph 2. of this Article and in accordance with Article 38, paragraph 3. of the LPFMA.

#### Article 21

Issuance of securities

\1. For the purpose of issuing domestic state debt, the Minister as the sole authorized individual to enter into state debts, within the budget year 2026 within the amount provided for the issuance of domestic debt in Table 1, shall issue securities under the conditions set out in the respective law on state debt and sub-legal acts deriving from this law.

\2. However, the amount required for the issuance of securities within the limit defined in paragraph 1. of this Article, may be subject to review depending on the dynamics of budget

### LAW NO. 10/L-001 ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO FOR YEAR 2026

execution and available funding, as assessed by the Minister. For this purpose, the Minister shall be authorized to replace the structure of state debt instruments, within the maximum limits of state debt issuance set out in Tables 1 and 1.1 attached to this Law.

\3. Pursuant to the relevant Law on State Debt and Guarantees, the Ministry shall be authorized to refinance, through the issuance of securities, all existing instruments that mature within the fiscal year, unless otherwise provided by the securities calendar. The Ministry shall be authorized to use the Kosovo Fund for refinancing management according to the securities calendar in accordance with the cash flow plans for the fiscal year.

#### Article 22

Economic Recovery Program

\1. Through the Economic Recovery Program, the funds shall be allocated according to the proposal by the Minister and approval by the Government, based on the implementation plan approved by the Government. The funds allocated from all sources of funding shall be transferred and allocated to the respective expenditure category, under the relevant budgetary sub-program and the BO responsible for implementation, in accordance with the approved plan.

These budget moves shall not be subject to the transfer restrictions contained in Article 30 of the LPFMA or Article 14 of this Law.

\2. In cases when funds are allocated within the budget of the Ministry of Finance, Labour and Transfers, under the sub-program Treasury of Kosovo, to be transferred to a non-budgetary organization, then the Treasury shall be authorized to transfer funds to the beneficiary foreseen in the implementation plan according to paragraph 1. of this Article, after signing the agreement by the Minister and the beneficiary.

\3. Funds from the Economic Recovery Program shall not be used to pay court fees or other similar compensations to which BOs, independent agencies, or public enterprises are exposed.

#### Article 23

Lending to public entities, capitalisation and buying of shares

\1. The Ministry of Finance, Labour and Transfers, with the prior approval of Government, has the right to lend to any entity in the public sector that meets the conditions and criteria defined according to the legislation in force, up to the amount specified in Table 1.1. This limitation does not apply to loans sub-loaned to public entities under the relevant law on state debt.

\2. The Ministry of Finance, Labour and Transfers, with the prior approval of Government, has the right to negotiate and use the planned funds for Capitalisation and Buying of Shares up to the specified amount in Table 1.1., with the aim of capitalising (increasing the charter capital) for Sovereign Fund or capitalisation or buying of shares in enterprises or initiatives in the field of defence and security, aviation, and energy.

### LAW NO. 10/L-001 ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO FOR YEAR 2026

#### Article 24

Borrowing for potential projects and existing projects

\1. Funds from the sub-program Borrowing for Potential Projects and Existing Projects, within the Ministry of Finance, Labour and Transfers, which are funds from the source of financing external borrowing, Investment Clause and financing within the deficit limit, can be allocated for new projects or even existing ones, which are financed by international agreements.

\2. For new projects, according to the proposal from the Minister, the means are transferred with the approval of the Government, from the budget allocation according to paragraph 1. of this Article. The funds allocated from this source of financing are transferred to the corresponding expenditure category, to the relevant budgetary sub-program and to the BO responsible for implementation. These budget movements are not subject to the transfer restrictions contained in Article 30 of the LPFMA or Article 14 of this law.

\3. After such approval by the Government, the Minister is authorized to adapt the tables according to Article 4 and 5 of this law, giving a specific project code, in which the allocation of borrowing funds is made, after the ratification and entry into force of the loan agreement, in accordance with the legislation in force.

\4. For existing projects, if the dynamics of their execution is faster than planned, according to the proposal by the Minister, the means are transferred with approval from the Government, from the budget allocation according to paragraph 1. of this Article. The funds allocated from this source of financing are transferred to the corresponding expenditure category, to the relevant budgetary sub-program and to the BO responsible for implementation. These budget movements are not subject to the transfer restrictions contained in Article 30 of the LPFMA or Article 14 of this law. In case it is needed, with Government approval, the expenditure limit can be increased for ratified projects in the Assembly that are part of Investment Clause and do not exceed deficit ceiling according to fiscal rule.

#### Article 25

VAT for borrowing projects

\1. Within the VAT sub-program for borrowing funded projects, funds shall be allocated to cover VAT, in cases where such taxes are not covered by the lender.

\2. According to the request from the implementing BO of the borrowing project, with the approval of the Minister, the funds from this program shall be allocated and transferred to the corresponding expenditure category in the corresponding budget (sub) program. These budget movements shall be made excluding the limitation in Article 30 of the LPFMA, Article 14 and 15 of this Law.

### LAW NO. 10/L-001 ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO FOR YEAR 2026

#### Article 26

The adjustment of budget tables with regulations on internal systematization After the approval of the regulations for the internal organization of public institutions according to the requirements of Law No. 06/L-113 on the Organization and Functioning of the State Administration and Independent Agencies, the Ministry of Finance, Labour and Transfers shall be authorized to make the necessary adjustments to the budget tables of this Law, if there are no additional budget implications and additional number of employee positions.

#### Article 27

Authorization to use ‘Special Drawing Rights (SDR)’

\1. The Ministry of Finance, Labour and Transfers and the Central Bank of the Republic of Kosovo shall be authorized, in case of allocation by the International Monetary Fund of „Special Drawing Rights (SDR)‟ for the Republic of Kosovo, to carry out the process of their use through a Memorandum of Understanding, according to the needs of the budget of the Republic of Kosovo, through the CBK as a fiscal agent, pursuant to Article 4 of the Law No. 03/L-152 on Membership of the Republic of Kosovo in the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank Group Organizations.

\2. The Ministry of Finance, Labour and Transfers may use these funds according to the need and purpose as assessed by the Minister, which for the used part will be considered a state debt, in accordance with the relevant law on state debt, respectively international debt. The deadline for the return of these funds in the form of a medium-term loan shall be set out in the Memorandum of Understanding.

\3. All expenses arising from the use of this debt under paragraph 2. of this Article shall be calculated as costs of state debt and shall be transferred from the Budget of the Republic of Kosovo.

#### Article 28

Increasing the quota of the Republic of Kosovo

\1. It is authorized the payment of capital in the respective amount for International Financial Organizations where the Republic of Kosovo is a member in case of increased share quota.

\2. After approval by the Government, the Kosovo Treasury is authorized to proceed with the transfer of funds in the respective amount from the bank balance of the Treasury Single Account and shall present and recognize the same as financial assets of the Republic of Kosovo.

### LAW NO. 10/L-001 ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO FOR YEAR 2026

#### Article 29

Transfer of Funds Budgeted to the Diplomatic and Consular Missions

\1. The transfer of funds to Diplomatic and Consular Missions (including attachés) shall be performed by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Diaspora according to the approved budget, and shall be regulated by a special procedure.

\2. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Diaspora is obliged to supervise the accounts of Diplomatic and Consular Missions and to take care of the stable financing of the diplomatic activities of the Republic of Kosovo.

\3. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Diaspora is obliged to ensure accountability and transparency in the accounting records for the funds transferred to the Diplomatic and Consular Missions.

#### Article 30

Value of salary coefficient, allowances and compensations

\1. Monetary value of coefficient for the Law on Salaries in Public Sector is one hundred and ten (110 €) euros.

\2. The Minister is authorized to, as necessary, by decision, raise the ceiling of the allowances and compensations defined by the Law on Salaries in the Public Sector for fiscal year 2026.

#### Article 31

Calculation of Salaries in Public Sector

\1. The increase of one (1) unit in the salary coefficient, implemented by Law No. 08/L-332 on Budget Appropriations for the Budget of the Republic of Kosovo for the fiscal year 2025, for all job classes according to Annexes 1-15 of the Law No. 08/L-196 on Salaries in the Public Sector, shall continue to remain in effect for the fiscal year 2026.

\2. In accordance with the Judgment of the Constitutional Court KO79/23, instead of regulating according to paragraph 6. of Article 6 of the Law No.08/L-196 on Salaries in the Public Sector, the basic salary will increase based on work experience, by zero point five percent (0.5%) for each full year of work, starting from January 1, 2026.

#### Article 32

Payment of the 13th Salary for the Public Sector

\1. The Government may, during the fiscal year, through early allocation by decision, ensure the funds for the payment of the 13th salary in accordance with paragraph 2. of this Article. The Government must ensure that, throughout the fiscal year, the fiscal rule on not exceeding the deficit ceiling of 2% of the Gross Domestic Product is respected.

### LAW NO. 10/L-001 ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO FOR YEAR 2026

\2. If the conditions set out in paragraph 1. of this Article are met, the 13th salary for each employee will be an amount equal to the corresponding coefficient level multiplied by the value of the coefficient, excluding allowances, as defined by Law No. 08/L-196 on Salaries in the Public Sector. This will be granted to each public sector employee who has been employed in any budgetary organization for at least twelve (12) months before the month in which the decision is made. The conditions that must be met to qualify for the 13th salary and other eligibility criteria may be determined by a decision of the Government.

#### Article 33

Allocation and management of appropriations in the category of wages and allowances

\1. The allocation of funds needed for the payment of salaries until the end of the fiscal year for all filled positions must be carried out by the budget organization within thirty (30) days after the approval of the Law on Budget Appropriations. The allocation must include the amount required for the basic salary, work experience allowance, transitional allowance, employer‟s pension contribution, as well as any other approved allowance that is valid until the end of the fiscal year.

\2. In the absence of action by the Budget Organization in accordance with paragraph 1. of this Article, Treasury implements the approved budget for the expenditure category, wages and allowances in accordance with annual planning and cash flow, allocating each month one twelfth (1/12) of the approved annual budget for this category.

\3. The approval of hours for on-call duty, night work, and work outside regular working hours, as well as any other allowance or compensation provided under Law No. 08/L-196 on Salaries in the Public Sector, is conditional upon the availability of budgetary funds and must include the appropriate allocation of financial resources for the payment of that financial obligation by the end of the fiscal year. The approval of such allowance or compensation without authorization in accordance with the corresponding budget tables shall be considered unlawful.

\4. The budget allocated for unfilled job positions may be used exclusively for new job positions that are filled during the fiscal year within that budget organization.

\5. Any request by budget organizations for changes to the salary list, including job positions, coefficients, allowances or other compensations, may be submitted only in accordance with the budgeted allocations and the corresponding tables generated from the budget system - BDMS.

Otherwise, such action shall be considered unlawful.

\6. The approved budget for the expenditure category wages and allowances may not be used for other budgetary purposes, including the execution of court decisions.

### LAW NO. 10/L-001 ON BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR THE BUDGET OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOSOVO FOR YEAR 2026

#### Article 34

Financial obligations for membership in international institutions The financial obligations of the Republic of Kosovo for membership in international institutions shall be paid from the Treasury, from the bank balance, based on the obligations and membership agreement with the respective international institution, after approval by the Government.

#### Article 35

Implementation of progressive tax rate on immovable property The implementation of the progressive tax rate on immovable property according to Article 9 of the Law No. 06/L-005, supplemented and amended by Law No. 08/L-224, shall be postponed and shall start to be implemented from the tax year 2027. For the tax year 2026, the Transitional Tax Rate continues to be applied as provided for under Article 39 /A of the Law No. 06/L-005, supplemented and amended by Law No. 08/L-224.

#### Article 36

Expiration of the Budget of the Republic of Kosovo All budgetary appropriations for the fiscal year 2026 shall expire at midnight on 31 December 2026, except for undistributed budget appropriations from own source revenues of municipalities or any other BO permitted by this Law, which shall be carried forward to the following year.

#### Article 37

Entry into force This Law shall enter into force on the day of its publication in the Official Gazette of the Republic of Kosovo, with financial effect from 1 January 2026.

Law No.10/L- 001 20 February 2026

Promulgated by Decree No. DL-23/2026 dated 27.02.2026 President of the Republic of Kosovo Vjosa Osmani-Sadriu
